newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania profits fall but market share up.
newsitem.headline: Scania profits fall but market share up.

text.p: Swedish truck and bus maker Scania on Thursday reported a 39 percent fall in nine months profits after financial items, but said order intake in Europe was flat and market share had increased.
Scania posted a profit of 2.14 billion crowns after financial items compared to 3.51 billion in the same 1995 period. Sales totalled 24.57 billion crowns for the period compared to 25.44 billion.
"Scania's order intake from European markets for trucks was at about the same level as in the third quarter of 1995," the company said in its results statement.
Scania said its order intake in the first nine months fell to 26,539 trucks from 29,563. Invoicing fell to 28,799 trucks from 29,156.
It said its market share in western Europe rose slightly to 15.4 percent from 14.4 percent. In Brazil, Scania's market share increased to 37.5 percent from 33.9 percent.
The appreciation of the Swedish currency had cut into profits, Scania said.
"The stronger Swedish crown negatively affected the result by 720 crowns."
Scania said the third quarter of this year had been an intensive transition period to its 4-series trucks from the older 3-series.
"The costs for the production transition to the 4-series was 450 million crowns, of which 300 million was taken during the third quarter."
"Transition to the 4-series in European production facilities is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter," it added.
It said costs for the changeover in Europe had been estimated at 500 million crowns for 1996.
Scania said the changeover process had resulted in loss of some orders for the 4-series.

"During the report period, the changeover in the European production system from the 3-series to the 4-series limited Scania's ability to offer its customers all the planned specification alternatives in the 4-series."
"Order bookings were negatively affected by this."
It said fourth quarter earnings would also be affected by the changeover.
"The sharp increase in the number of variants of 4-series trucks during the period made the production changeover more difficult.
"As a result, the actual shortfall in production was approximately 500 vehicles greater than expected, and this influenced third quarter sales and earnings."
Britain remained Scania's largest market where 4,487 trucks were registered, up from 4,105. There Scania improved its market share to 18.2 percent from 16.7 percent.
Scania introduced its new generation of buses in September.
Order bookings for buses fell to 2,501 units from 3,328. Sales totalled 3,073 buses compared to 3,143.
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003
